spec_notes: The spec (ratchet/spec.md) does not contradict the request. It decides many unsaid points in ordinary clauses with 'implied' or 'existing' sources rather than marking them as choices: 409 for a no-op on a resolved/closed ticket (C-5), no notice on clearing (C-19), one notice per assignment even for the same agent (C-21/C-22), keeping the assignee through every transition (C-14), rejecting assignee on POST/PATCH (C-14). It marks as Open for the requester points the product then decides anyway and documents in docs/api.md: name normalisation and counting (C-2: kept verbatim, UTF-16 units), case and spacing in the filter (C-27: exact), repeated assignee parameters (C-30: first value), assignee in list --raw (C-36: not added). It pins choices a correct product need not share: exact retry waits 1/2/4/8 s (C-24), body-size endpoints and MAX_BODY_BYTES start limits (C-8, C-46), save-failure rollback with an identical retry (C-43), CLI history quoting (C-49, C-51). The product does not meet its own C-52 (malformed byte in the filter must not match a U+FFFD name).
tests_notes: The new tests are few and very broad: 'assigns, hands off and clears ...' checks assignment, handoff, clearing, null no-op, repeat no-op, updated, audit actor, ticket shape on create/list/PATCH/transition and the outbox in one test; 'assignee, status and priority intersect ...' covers both filters, intersection, cursor paging, repeated parameters, case and invalid values; a failure names little. Tied to internals: the save-failure test creates a directory at `${dataFile}.${process.pid}.tmp` (the persistence temp-file name); CLI tests build data through TicketStore.assign() and createPersistence; one mocks fs.renameSync; one calls readJson with the strictUtf8 option directly; delivery tests call service.worker.tick() and service.notifier.deliver(). Would fail on another correct build: exact 200 + full ticket on PUT, 409 on a no-op to a resolved ticket, surrounding spaces kept in names (' Dana + R&D '), 33 emoji refused (UTF-16 counting), no notice on clear, ticket.assigned as the action for clearing, quoted names and the word unassigned in the CLI table and history text, POST/PATCH refusing assignee, separate outbox keys for each assignment. No test checks package.json for dependencies.
maintainer: store.assign() is the only change with its own snapshot-and-restore path around apply(), and the assignment notice key is built from the audit entry's seq, so the outbox, audit log and persistence are coupled in a way the other store methods are not; changing apply() or the key scheme safely means reading the rollback and the regression tests together. The name rule (isAssigneeName: untrimmed, UTF-16 count, no control or separator characters) differs from the trimmed text() rule for titles and requesters and is shared by validation, the filter and data-file loading, so tightening it can make existing data files refuse to load.
